html:
Sarmizegetusa Regia was the capital and main religious centre of the Dacian kingdom, built on terraces about 1,200 metres high in the Orăștie Mountains of Transylvania in the first century BCE.

It lay at the heart of a ring of hill forts that guarded the kingdom of Burebista and later Decebalus. Its sacred area held round and rectangular sanctuaries of stone and wooden posts, one of them often read as a calendar. Workshops, houses and water pipes spread over the slopes. The Romans took and destroyed it in Trajan's wars, ending the independent kingdom of Dacia, and built a garrison there. Its remains, with the other Dacian fortresses of the Orăștie Mountains, are a World Heritage Site.
sum: Sarmizegetusa Regia was the capital and main religious centre of the Dacian kingdom, built on terraces about 1,200 metres high in the Orăștie Mountains of Transylvania in the first century BCE.
